title: Binaries (<<...>>) vs. Character Lists, UTF-8 & Zero-Copy IOLists
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates 16x memory savings of binaries over character lists, nested zero-copy IOList construction for HTTP, and iolist_size/iolist_to_binary handling.

Calculates the size of an iolist in bytes without allocating or flattening.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does gen_tcp:send(Socket, [HeaderBin, BodyBin]) outperform concatenating <<HeaderBin/binary, BodyBin/binary>> before sending?

options.label: The BEAM passes the IOList pointers directly to the OS kernel writev() system call, streaming the disjoint buffers onto the network wire without allocating a copy in RAM
options.explanation: Scatter-gather I/O bypasses user-space buffer concatenation completely.

options.label: The IOList is automatically compressed by the Erlang compiler before transmission
options.explanation: IOLists are not compressed; they are emitted as disjoint memory vectors.

options.label: Because Erlang sockets only support linked lists, not binaries
options.explanation: Erlang sockets support raw binaries, iolists, and iodata.
